title: Slurry storage: sort it in summer, be winter-ready

content.content: In the middle of another hot, dry summer we can see our climate is changing. When we head into winter this translates into more rain, more runoff, and more pressure on slurry storage.  Getting ahead now can help protect your land, your business and the waterways your community depends on.

Slurry managed well is a resource. Slurry mismanaged is a pollution risk - to rivers, soils, and the communities downstream. The choices made now, in summer, shape what happens to those waterways come January.
At the Environment Agency we’re encouraging farmers to look at slurry storage requirements before the rain arrives. Now is the time to start planning for next winter.
With pressure on fuel and fertiliser prices, having plenty of spare capacity is not only vital for compliance, but also saves a valuable resource for when it’s most needed.
From an environmental point of view, spreading slurry during the winter months creates a significant pollution risk from run-off, damages soils and wastes valuable nutrients.
Spreading because your store is full, rather than because there is a soil or crop need, is also non-compliant with environmental regulations.
How much slurry storage capacity do I need?
The Silage, Slurry and Fuel Oil Regulations set out that all farms must have at least 4 months slurry storage.
If you’re in a Nitrate Vulnerable Zone, that requirement is higher.  Check what applies to your livestock type.
Farming Rules for Water also say you should not apply more than the soil and crop actually need, and you should not create a pollution risk.
We recommend a minimum of 6 months slurry storage to ensure meeting the requirements of Farming Rules for Water.
What can I do to prepare my slurry storage for winter?

Guttering that leaks or drainage that isn’t functioning properly can lead to an increase in slurry volume as clean rainwater mixes with manure in yards. Fixing any leaky pipes and gutters and making sure drains are free and running properly can make a difference. You may find these changes alone mean that your existing storage meets your requirements.
Use the AHDB slurry wizard to check how much slurry storage you need – this will show you if have enough storage to be compliant and to see you through the winter.
It can also help with planning for the future to assess the levels of capacity you may need for farm expansion, or to give you a buffer for contingency.
If your calculations show that you may not have enough storage, look at contingencies and get a plan in place to increase your storage capacity.
3. Plan for all eventualities
Whether you think you have enough storage capacity or not, making contingency plans could help you through if something unexpected happens.
Options to consider:

Read more about the guidance around storing slurry and planning a new store including notifying the Environment Agency at least 14 days before you build new storage for slurry or make substantial changes to an existing store.

Farmers can access Defra funding to improve slurry storage and management through the Capital Grant offer, expected to open 30 July. The Grant will fund items like automatic slurry scrapers, self-supporting covers for slurry and anaerobic digestate stores  and floating covers for slurry and anaerobic digestate stores and lagoons. Read the full guidance for Capital Grants here - Applicant's guide: Capital Grants 2026 - GOV.UK

Being ready for winter can help your business all year round. Only applying organic fertiliser during the growing season means that crops and grass take up more of the nutrients, increasing yields. Keeping machinery off wet soils not only protects the soil, but saves unnecessary fuel, wear and tear and man hours.
See how a Cornish dairy farmer tackles slurry storage challenges and transforms his farm to meet regulations.
Get in touch
If you have questions about preparing for winter, we can help – contact our national customer contact centre and ask to be put in contact with your local agriculture team.
Environment Agency National Customer Contact Centre
Email: enquiries@environment-agency.gov.uk
Other resources:
Farming Advice Service: https://www.farmingadviceservice.org.uk/technical-article/environment-agency-winter-ready-cab-card

title: New date for Capital Grants 2026 webinar

content.content: The 2026 Capital Grants is expected to open on 30 July.
To help you prepare, we're hosting a webinar on 30 July for you to find out more. This webinar has been rescheduled from the original date of 22 July.
During the session you'll hear from me, and colleagues from the Rural Payments Agency (RPA). We will also cover the support provided by Catchment Sensitive Farming (CSF) (look at section 4.2).
We will explain which grant items may need CSF advice before you apply, and RPA colleagues will take you through the application and claims process.
We'll finish with a Q&A session, giving you the chance to ask questions and get answers from the team.
The webinar will start at 11am and finish at 12:30pm.
Register to attend.
If you can’t make it, don’t worry. We will publish a link to the recording once the webinar finishes.
For more information ahead of the webinar, do read my previous posts on Capital Grants and the Capital Grants 2026 guidance on GOV.UK.
This new round will make £225 million available which is 50% more than in 2025.
I look forward to seeing you there.

description: To help you prepare to apply for Capital Grants 2026, we're hosting a webinar on Thursday 30 July for you to find out more.

title: Learn more about the Farmer Welfare Grant

content.content: Earlier this month, we wrote a post introducing the Farmer Welfare Grant.
A total of £1.5 million will be available over 3 years to support farmer mental health and wellbeing across England.
The funding is intended to help rural and agricultural charities and organisations deliver practical support that strengthens both personal and business resilience across the sector.

While the application portal will not open until 6 August, we are sharing additional information in advance to help organisations considering an application. This includes details of 2 upcoming webinars.
Guidance, including the technical eligibility criteria, will be available when the portal opens.
Who can apply
Funding is only available to organisations with experience of supporting farming communities, not for individual farm businesses.
Any charitable or third-sector not-for-profit organisation registered in England can apply for funding if it can demonstrate its ability to deliver a suitable project.

For-profit organisations may also be eligible to apply as part of a consortium led by an eligible organisation, provided they can demonstrate how both the project and their role contribute to meeting the funding criteria.

We want grant recipients to develop support that responds to the specific needs of farming communities. For this reason, we are not prescribing the types of activities or approaches applicants should propose.
That said, applications that support the following priorities are particularly encouraged:

Funding can be used to cover both one-off and ongoing costs. This may include overheads, venue hire, materials, equipment, service delivery costs, and staffing costs where these are directly related to the project.
The exact number of projects will be determined by the amount and nature of applications we receive.
We’ll consider both individual projects and joint projects involving multiple organisations.
Applications are invited for grants of between £1,000 and £200,000 per year, covering expenditure incurred between November 2026 and March 2029.
How to apply
To apply, you must do so through an application portal. We will blog again when the portal opens.

Once the application window has closed, the applications will be reviewed and scored by a team from Defra. Funding decisions will be made after all applications have been assessed.
Dates to note
Thursday 6 August – Application portal opens. Full guidance available.
Thursday 13 August, 2pm–3pm – Join our first webinar to learn more about the grant, guidance and eligibility criteria. A recording will be shared in this post after the session.
Monday 17 August, 10am–11am – Join our second webinar for a walkthrough of the application portal and application process. A recording will be shared in this post after the session
Wednesday 9 September, 11:59 am– Application portal closes.

By subscribing, you'll receive an email notification whenever we publish a new blog post.
